title: The DCLab intern: a chat mode with tools and a budget over the notebook
request: Build something like Hugging Face's ML Intern directly inside the R&D project, locally and one click away; fill the gaps (Kaggle and Hugging Face data, multiclass, time-series, imbalanced-fraud and text + tabular cases) and make finished work usable as SFT data.
spec: dclab_rnd/intern/: a toolbox with JSON schemas over the notebook and the evidence, an OpenAI-compatible client (OpenAI, the Hugging Face router, Ollama), a loop with a budget of tool calls and minutes, a standard plan when no model is configured, and stored sessions; routes under /api/intern; an Intern page and 'Hand to the intern' on every project. The expansion datasets join the sample picker; finished projects export as SFT examples. Done when tests/test_intern.py runs with a scripted model and no key.
plan: List the tools the intern may call: five evidence tools (search_evidence, get_record, get_rules, plan_next_stage, review_code) and thirteen project tools (list_samples, create_project, use_sample, describe_data, propose_contract, set_contract, set_settings, run_stage, run_all, approve_stage, get_results, ask_project, export_notebook).
Move the data attach and sample logic from the server into studio.data, so the intern and the API share one path.
Write the loop: in model mode the model writes a plan, calls tools and finishes with a report; with no model, the same tools run in the fixed DCLab order (sample, contract, five stages, report).
Enforce the budget on every step and record the minutes used per session.
Add the four expansion datasets (imbalanced card fraud, 26-class letters, daily bike demand, clothing reviews with text) to the sample picker with the contracts the campaign wrote for them.
Export a finished project as SFT examples (one per stage plus one for the contract) and add a Training examples button.
Build the Intern page (composer, budget, plan, tool-call transcript, report, follow-ups) and test the loop with a scripted model.

decisions.decision: Every tool is one the R&D verified, deterministic and bounded; the intern cannot run arbitrary code, reach the network or touch files outside the project home.
decisions.why: The difference from ML Intern is being right, not only automatic: the model never owns a split, a metric or a selection rule.

decisions.decision: A standard plan runs when no model is configured, and its transcript looks the same as a model's.
decisions.why: The product must work offline and in tests, and a person sees the same kind of session either way.

decisions.decision: The system prompt states five rules the intern never breaks: contract before any score, stages in order with the holdout consumed once, numbers with uncertainty and cited evidence, no production-readiness claims, stay inside the budget.
decisions.why: These are the repository's rules; the model must follow them through tool calls, and the deterministic code enforces what the prompt cannot.

decisions.decision: The client speaks the OpenAI-compatible API, so OpenAI, the Hugging Face router and a local Ollama all work.
decisions.why: The owner wants it local and one click away; one protocol covers paid and free models.

decisions.decision: Finished projects export as RAFT-style SFT examples.
decisions.why: The notebook then also becomes the data factory for the owner's future model.

decisions.decision: Tests use a scripted model, never a key.
decisions.why: A test must be repeatable and free; a live model makes it depend on the network and on rate limits.

change: New dclab_rnd/intern/ (tools.py with 18 tools, llm.py, loop.py with the budget and the standard plan, sessions.py with a default budget of 24 tool calls and 20 minutes); dclab_rnd/studio/sft.py and /api/projects/{id}/export/sft; studio.data gained attach_data, use_sample and the expansion samples; routes /api/intern and /api/intern/sessions; an Intern page and 'Hand to the intern'; tests/test_intern.py.

findings.defect: The minutes a session used were added up wrongly across turns.
findings.scenario: A session ran, then received a follow-up turn; the minutes recorded did not match the time actually spent, so the minutes budget was checked against a wrong number.
findings.cause: The turn's elapsed time was added to the running total without a fixed baseline for where the turn started.
findings.fix: Keep a minutes_before baseline when a turn starts and set minutes to that baseline plus the turn's elapsed time.
findings.test: Not covered by a dedicated test: test_budget_is_enforced checks the tool-call budget only.

findings.defect: The intern tests took about 35 seconds, too slow for the suite run before every commit.
findings.scenario: The standard-plan test and the API test each built a whole project on larger samples.
findings.cause: The tests used samples bigger than the behaviour under test needs.
findings.fix: Run the standard-plan test on the small heart disease sample and the API test on the bike sample; the file now takes about 11 seconds.

outcome: Done: a person can hand a task in plain language to the intern, which plans, calls the verified tools under a budget and reports; it works with no model through the standard plan. Later found: the API test read the developer's .env key and called a live model (fixed in package 0.1).
lessons: An agent's edge is the tools it is allowed to call: give it only verified, bounded tools and keep splits, metrics and selection in code.
A deterministic fallback plan with the same transcript shape keeps the product usable offline and the tests free.
A test of an agent must own its environment; a key present on the machine silently turns a scripted test into a live one.
